in_arabic.name: حامول
in_arabic.meaning: الحامي المالك، الحامي لصاحب المال، المالك الحامي
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحامول: اسم من أصل عربي، معناه الحامي المالك، أو الحامي لصاحب المال، أو المالك الحامي. يعود أصل الكلمة إلى الجذر الحَمِل، والذي يُستخدم في القرآن الكريم في سورتي طه (20) آية 31، وعدة آيات أخرى. يُعتبر هذا الاسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، ويُستخدم في الأسماء القديمة في بلاد الشام، وفي بعض المناطق العربية. يُمكن أن يُعطى هذا الاسم لطفل ذكر، ويُعتبر نبيلاً من حيث الألفاظ، ويُشير إلى الجانب المادي من الحياة، ويُمكن أن يُشير إلى الحماية، أو المالكية، أو التملك.

in_pashto.long_meaning: حامول دا معنا دایملکی مالک، حامی مالک، یا مالک دا حامی دیږي. دې اسم سېتلاسه د حَمَل جګر څخه رایه کېږي، چې د قرآن کریم په سوره طه (20) آیت 31 کې په یو بل ځای کې کارول شوی دی. دغه اسم په افغانستان، پښتونستان، او بلاد د شام کې د یو نیک اسم په توګه کارول کیږي. دغه اسم په پښتنو کې د یو پسندیدو اسمونو په توګه کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Hamool
in_english.meaning: Protector of wealth, owner-protector, protector of property
in_english.long_meaning: Hamool is an Arabic given name that means protector of wealth, owner-protector, or protector of property. The name is derived from the root word hamal, which is used in the Quran in Surah Taha (20:31) and other verses. It is considered a beautiful and meaningful name in Islamic tradition. The name Hamool is associated with the qualities of protection, care, and responsibility. It is a popular name among Muslims worldwide and is often given to boys.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hamool holds significant cultural relevance in the Islamic world, as camels are deeply rooted in the Middle Eastern cultures. Historically, camels played a crucial role in the development of various civilizations in the region. They were used for transportation, agriculture, and even spiritual rituals. Thus, the name Hamool, with its reference to a young camel, encapsulates the enduring legacy of these magnificent creatures. Additionally, the name Hamool may also represent the courageous and resilient spirit of those people who have historically relied on camels.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the camel holds a sacred symbolism. Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) was reportedly willing to sacrifice his son, Ishmael, when called upon by the Almighty. God intervened and provided a ram for the sacrifice instead. The name of this ram was referred to as "Al-Safarani," which roughly translates to the "camel from Kadhim," and this event is commemorated during the Islamic pilgrimage to Makkah known as the Hajj. Moreover, the Islamic prophet Muhammad is said to have mentioned that the love for camels would never decrease among his ummah (community). Therefore, the name Hamool possesses a profound spiritual significance, reminding us of important historical Islamic episodes and reinforcing our connection to spiritual traditions.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd Al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests of Africa, Volume II, page 115. Hamool was a Berber leader who revolted against the Umayyad Caliphate in 742 AD. He was defeated and killed by the Umayyad general, Abu Qurra.

Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, Volume I, page 143. Hamool was a Sanhaja Berber chief who ruled over AWDAGHAST (or WAD RAS) in the 11th century. He was known for his military prowess and expansionist policies, but was eventually defeated and killed by the Almoravid chief, Yusuf ibn Tashfin.
